system.name: FuseFlow
system.one_liner: a fusion-centric compiler converting sparse PyTorch models into fused sparse dataflow graphs for reconfigurable dataflow architectures

components.name: PyTorch Model
components.role: input model source (e.g., sparse matmuls and linear layers) to be compiled

components.name: Einsum expressions w/ optional user schedules and sparse formats
components.role: intermediate representation extending the model with non-algebraic operators, schedules (red) and sparse formats (green)

components.name: Fused Einsum Expressions
components.role: cross-expression fused representation grouping fusable operators into a connected subgraph

components.name: Partial-Order Graph (POG)
components.role: graph encoding index/iteration-order constraints derived from schedules and sparse formats for the fused region

components.name: Fusion Table
components.role: new IR encoding fused iteration order (rows), fused tensors (columns) and IR nodes/stream pointers (cells) for lowering fused expressions

components.name: SAMML Fused Dataflow Graph
components.role: generated hardware-ready sparse dataflow graph with ML primitives, targeting simulation, FPGA or a pruning heuristic

flows.to: Einsum expressions w/ optional user schedules and sparse formats
flows.what: lowering via Torch-MLIR/MPACT with user schedules and formats

flows.from: Einsum expressions w/ optional user schedules and sparse formats

flows.what: evaluation targets: Dataflow Simulator, FPGA, Heuristic (Section 8)

content.key_idea: FuseFlow lowers a PyTorch model to Einsum expressions carrying user schedules and sparse formats, fuses them across kernel boundaries into a partial-order graph, encodes the fused computation in a novel tabular fusion-table IR, and generates a hardware-ready sparse dataflow graph for simulation or FPGA/CGRA backends.
content.reading_order: Left to right across the top row (a-c): PyTorch model, Einsum expressions, fused expressions with partial-order graph; then down and left to right across the bottom row (d-e): fusion table, SAMML fused dataflow graph feeding evaluation.

summary: FuseFlow is a compiler that converts sparse PyTorch models into fused sparse dataflow graphs for reconfigurable dataflow architectures (RDAs), supporting general cross-expression fusion of sparse operations. This figure walks through FuseFlow's full compilation pipeline in five lettered panels. (a) A PyTorch model with sparse and dense operators is (b) lowered via Torch-MLIR/MPACT into Einsum expressions annotated with optional user schedules (red) and sparse tensor formats (green). (c) Cross-expression kernel fusion (Section 5) merges user-marked Fuse{} regions into a connected fused-Einsum subgraph plus a partial-order graph encoding index constraints. (d) A new fusion-table IR (Section 6) encodes the fused iteration order in its rows, fused tensors in its columns, and IR nodes/stream pointers in its cells, addressing the need to reference temporary streams across fused kernels. (e) Code generation from the fusion table produces a SAMML fused dataflow graph, which is evaluated via a cycle-accurate Dataflow Simulator, an FPGA backend, or a fast pruning heuristic.
summary_zh: 该图分五个面板展示FuseFlow编译流程：(a) PyTorch模型经Torch-MLIR/MPACT降级为(b) 带用户调度（红）与稀疏格式（绿）标注的Einsum表达式；(c) 跨表达式核融合生成融合子图与偏序图；(d) 新提出的融合表IR编码融合迭代顺序与张量流指针；(e) 代码生成得到SAMML融合数据流图，供仿真器、FPGA或启发式方法评估。
